Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ right-handed man with history 
of composite Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS 
recurrence who is being admitted for his ___ cycle of high-dose 
methotrexate.  

(1) Lymphoma with CNS Recurrence:  Patient received his ___ 
cycle of high-dose methotrexate and was rescued with leucovorin 
20 mg q6 hours.  His urine pH was maintained > or = 8.0.  His 
creatinine remained stable at 0.8.  However, his LFTs did 
increase, prompting an increase in IVF with bicarb and 
leucovorin dosing. LFTs peaked and trended down before 
discharge. He did have a brain MRI which showed no new lesions. 
Next cycle scheudled for ___.

unchanged from baseline and he did well with artificial tears.

methotrexate chemotherapy. You tolerated the therapy well, with 
minimal side effects. While here you had an MRI of your brain 
which showed no evidence of recurrent tumors.

You should restart your daily 81mg aspirin tablet, which was 
being held leading up to this hospitalization. Continue your 
other home medicines. You do not need to take any new 
prescription medications. You should come back on ___ for

If you have any fever, chills, decreased urine output, or any 
worrisome symptoms, please call your oncologist or primary care 
physician or go to the Emergency Department.

radiology_notes.text:
MRI HEAD.

___ and ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar multisequence MR images of the head were obtained
before and after the administration of IV gadolinium.

FINDINGS:  There are no intracranial masses or areas of abnormal enhancement.
Again seen is a small T2-hyperintense focus involving the left posterior
frontal lobe with small areas of susceptibility consistent with old blood
products from prior biopsy.

There are scattered small subcortical white matter T2-hyperintense foci which
likely represent chronic microangiopathic changes.  The ventricles and extra-
axial CSF spaces are normal and unchanged.

The visualized orbits and major flow voids are normal.  Soft tissue changes of
the left maxillary sinus are seen.

Again seen is a left parietal burr hole.

IMPRESSION:  No significant change since ___ with no evidence of
recurrent tumors.  No significant change in the small T2-hyperintense focus in
the left posterior frontal lobe which likely represents gliosis.
